$schema_note: THE marketing-agents (OGMC) TENANT SCHEMA, RECONSTRUCTED FROM COMMITTED SOURCE FOR A FULLY-OFFLINE LOCAL DEV STACK (bd startsim-768w.69). NOT a delta like scripts/schemas/ogmc.json and not a hand-guess: the spine of this payload is a COMMITTED, READ-ONLY CAPTURE of the live declaration. start-simpli-api/tenant-starter/apps/api/tests/test_agent_account_isolation.py carries LIVE_TYPES / LIVE_RELATIONSHIPS, described in its own module docstring as 'the LIVE marketing-agents declaration, read with a read-only GET /api/v1/schema/{types,attributes,relationships}/ on 2026-09-16 and replayed here through the same public endpoints a foundry uses'. Every type key, attribute name, data_type, enum choice list, required flag, config.scope block and relationship end below is taken from that capture unless its own note says otherwise. Nothing here was read from the network: the live tenant was never contacted (no QA credential exists for it and its AWS secret is marked for deletion), so this file is reconstruction from the tree alone.
corroboration_note: THE CAPTURE IS NOT THE ONLY WITNESS, and the second ones matter because they were taken on DIFFERENT DAYS through a different route — so an attribute present in both is not one capture's typo. (1) marketing-agents-web/src/components/__tests__/record-columns.test.ts holds TOPIC_ATTRS (17), DRAFT_ATTRS (15) and NEWS_ATTRS (19) 'in the order the tenant API returns it (read off GET /api/v1/schema/types on the live tenant 2026-09-07)' — name and ORDER only, no data types. (2) marketing-agents-web/src/lib/__tests__/topic-edit.test.ts holds 'the live marketing-agents `topic` type (GET /api/v1/schema/types/, 2026-09-23)' WITH data types, and it matches the 2026-09-16 capture attribute for attribute. (3) marketing-agents-web/src/lib/__tests__/draft-translation.test.ts and approval-translation.test.ts both record the draft type 'read off the LIVE marketing-agents tenant on 2026-08-19 (ECS exec, inside org_scope("marketing-agents"))' with data types, plus 'rel defs — grounded_by, for_client, written_for, translation_of'. The three draft readings agree, and the one difference between them is accounted for: the 2026-08-19 and 2026-09-07 readings carry 15 draft attributes and the 2026-09-16 one carries 16, the extra being `topic_ref` — exactly the attribute scripts/schemas/ogmc.json declared on 2026-09-07 while saying it 'leaves the other fifteen attributes exactly as they are'. ATTRIBUTE ORDER HERE IS THE CAPTURED ORDER, which is load-bearing beyond cosmetics: record-columns.ts caps a table's default columns at six in the type's own attribute order (DEFAULT_ATTR_CAP), and health-data.ts::intakeStage is choicesOf(status)[0], so reordering silently changes which columns open and which stage counts as intake.
org_note: Schema rows are per-org and org_id comes from the JWT claim, so this applies to whichever org the token acts as; there is no --org flag. Apply to a LOCAL stack with:  python3 scripts/declare_tenant_schema.py --schema <this file> --base-url http://127.0.0.1:<port> --token "$TOKEN"  . AND THEN RUN  manage.py redenormalize_attributes --org <org> --type <each type>  IF ANY ROWS ALREADY EXIST: denormalize_attributes runs on WRITE, so rows already on disk carry no core_attribute row for a newly declared name and every attr.<name> filter answers count: 0 over a corpus full of matches — indistinguishable from not having declared it at all. That silence is what produced three production defects in one day on this tenant (scripts/schemas/ogmc.json, bd startsim-8hgmq.3/.4/.11). On a freshly seeded local stack there is nothing to backfill and the step is a no-op.
access_note: `access: {}` ON EVERY TYPE IS A DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE FROM THE CAPTURE, and it is the one place this payload is not a transcription. The 2026-09-16 capture carries `access` on `scope` ALONE; the other five types declare no access key and therefore resolve, per tenant-starter/apps/schema_registry/access.py step 3, to the org baseline — any member of the org reads them. For a single-user local dev stack `{}` resolves to the SAME read (org-wide, no row scope) and additionally PINS it, so a later org-wide `*` posture cannot narrow a type the dev stack depends on. It is also below the policy-admin gate: access.py::declares_policy tests TRUTHINESS, so `{"access": {}}` does not need TENANT_POLICY_ADMIN_MIN_ROLE and a plain token can apply this file. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT IS `row_scope`. The same test file's isolate() PATCHes `access: {"row_scope": "scope", ...}` onto draft/topic/scope — that is the TEST'S CONFIGURATION UNDER TEST (bd startsim-rjl3b), not part of the live declaration it replays, and copying it here would hide every row from the single local dev user unless that user held a core_grant on each scope container. A local stack that opens empty is worse than no stack. ONE CONDITION ON APPLYING THIS TO A STACK THAT IS NOT FRESH: access.py::declaration_widens_reads refuses a declaration 'by EFFECT rather than by spelling' when an empty policy would replace an org default that declares a row_scope — but it asks 'would declaring this let some role read records that ALREADY EXIST and that it cannot read today?', so it is a check on the TRANSITION over EXISTING ROWS. On a fresh offline stack with no reserved `*` type and no rows it cannot fire. Against an already-seeded stack that has given `*` a row_scope, these five `access: {}` blocks are the thing that would be refused; drop the `access` key from those five types (leaving `scope` alone, which the live tenant declares) and the payload reverts to the capture exactly.
views_note: NO `config.views` BLOCK ON ANY TYPE, and that is a finding rather than a gap. The 2026-09-16 capture carries exactly two reserved config keys — `scope` and (on the scope type) `access` — and no `views` on any of the six types, so declaring one would be inventing presentation this tenant has never declared. It also is not needed: marketing-agents-web INFERS presentation from data types today (src/lib/board.ts::pickStatusAttr / typeRoute, pinned by src/lib/__tests__/nav-active.test.ts, whose fixture comments read 'Declares status, so typeRoute makes its nav href the BOARD, not the table' and 'no enum -> table'), which is precisely the inference tenant-starter/apps/schema_registry/type_views.py was written to replace on tenants that opt in. marketing-agents has not opted in. Nothing in the app source names which type would hold `board.primary`, and that key is capped at one per org, so guessing it would plant a dashboard pipeline nobody asked for. No views block was dropped for failing validation — none was written.
underscore_keys_note: THE `_`-PREFIXED KEYS ARE DATA-BLOB-ONLY AND ARE NOT DECLARED HERE. `_origin`, `_trigger`, `_triggered_by`, `_run_id` (marketing-agents-web/src/lib/draft-origin.ts) and `_edit_history` (src/lib/edit-history.ts) are stamped INSIDE Entity.data by the n8n writer and by this app, and all three modules say in words that they are rendered and never filtered: draft-origin.ts — 'THESE ARE RENDERED, NOT FILTERABLE... `_trigger` is not a declared attribute on the draft type... NEVER add ?attr._trigger='; edit-history.ts — '`_edit_history` is not a declared attribute on the draft type... NEVER add ?attr._edit_history='; drafts-view.ts — '`_triggered_by` is not a declared attribute on the draft type'. The 2026-09-16 capture confirms it: not one of the five appears in LIVE_TYPES. They also do not appear in the 2026-09-07 or 2026-08-19 readings. So they are blob keys, not AttributeDefs, and declaring them would make each a generated column and spend a slot in record-columns.ts's six-column default cap for a value no filter may use.

IT IS SUPERSEDED, NOT USED. Its six attributes are byte-for-byte the per-client config fields of the generic `scope` type (name/brand_voice/priority_framework/services/guardrails/active), and scripts/schemas/scope.json opens by saying the replacement is deliberate: 'ONE GENERIC SELF-NESTING TYPE, not client-and-project as two'. marketing-agents-web never reads it — the app's only listAllEntities calls are for topic, draft, news_item and source. config.note: SCOPED, which is the one of scoping.py's four states that makes ?scope= work. A non-empty string names the path attribute and the filter is applied; UNDECLARED (no key), UNSCOPED (null/""/{}) and MALFORMED all FAIL CLOSED with a 400. `scope_path` is the name marketing-agents-web/src/lib/scope.ts exports as SCOPE_PATH_ATTR ('Declared on the topic and draft types, and named ONCE here'), and the capture declares the same. `edge: draft_in_scope` is in the capture too and is why the reldef of that name is declared below: scoping.py's EDGE_KEY is OPTIONAL — a type with a path and no edge can still be READ by ?scope= but cannot be STAMPED on upsert, because there is no container type to resolve the path against — so omitting it would leave every locally-created draft unstampable and silently invisible to the scope-gated UI.

attributes.name: topic_ref
attributes.note: TEXT, NOT json, AND THE REASON IS WRITTEN DOWN. Copied from scripts/schemas/ogmc.json, which declared it live on 2026-09-07 and explains: 'the value is a uuid STRING, and value_column() sends json-typed attributes to value_json where an exact text match would never land'. It was written on 147 of 150 drafts by the n8n writer (buildStoryFromTopic, `topic_ref: String(topic.id)`) and declared on none of them, and the tenant answers a filter on an undeclared attribute by APPLYING it and matching nothing — count: 0, named in applied_filters and absent from ignored_filters. That silence produced three defects in one day: /t/draft opened empty for every user under a chip reading 'Topic approved' (startsim-8hgmq.4) and the server-side 'already has drafts' guard had a structurally zero count, so it relayed the writer twice for one topic 79 seconds apart (startsim-8hgmq.3). marketing-agents-web/src/lib/topic-drafts.ts names it ONCE as TOPIC_REF_ATTR; src/lib/drafts-view.ts and src/lib/topic-gate.ts both narrow with it only when declaresTopicRef() says the type declares it, which is why an offline stack that omits it is slow rather than silently empty. types.label: Scope
types.identity: external_id is `scope:<path>` — the path is the natural key, so an upsert that re-sends a scope lands on the same row. Re-parenting therefore CHANGES the external_id along with the path, and the mover does exactly that (bd startsim-hdtds, tenant-starter/apps/schema_registry/scope_moves.py): a scope row whose external_id ENDS WITH the path it is moving off has that suffix rewritten. Left stale it would be worse than cosmetic — the next re-send of the scope resolves on `scope:<new path>`, finds nothing, and creates a DUPLICATE scope at the new path beside the one that moved. The suffix guard is why a corpus row keyed on a URL is never touched by the same rule.
types.verbatim_note: COPIED VERBATIM FROM start-simpli-api/scripts/schemas/scope.json — types, config and all nine attributes with their own notes, plus the `parent_scope` relationship below. That file is the authoritative, already-committed declaration of the scope primitive (bd startsim-mwvwp, under epic startsim-ux39t) and NOTHING HERE WAS INVENTED OR RE-DERIVED. The 2026-09-16 live capture in tenant-starter/apps/api/tests/test_agent_account_isolation.py matches it attribute for attribute, including both `required` flags and the `path_attribute`/`parent_attribute` pair. scope.json's top-level `scoped_corpus_example` block is deliberately NOT lifted: it is documentation the test suite executes (tenant-starter/apps/api/tests/test_scope_primitive.py), spelled with a different path-attribute name on purpose, and merging its two-attribute `news_item` and its `in_scope` reldef would have overwritten this payload's real news_item with a worked example.
types.scope_key_note: `parent_attribute` NAMES THE MIRROR SO A MOVE CAN REWRITE IT (bd startsim-hdtds). `parent` is `path` minus its last segment, stored redundantly so `?attr.parent=/ogmc` answers 'the direct children' with no derivation — the first query a scope switcher issues. A rename that rewrote only `path` would leave every descendant's `parent` pointing at a container that no longer exists, and the switcher would draw the tree as it was. NO `edge` HERE, deliberately: a scope's own containment is `parent_scope`, which is a self-edge derived from `parent` rather than from a scope stamp, and a scope's `path` is NEW by definition — it is the one path that must not be required to name a container that already exists, or the first scope in a tenant could never be created.
types.config_note: `access: {}` is DELIBERATE, not a stub, and is the same reasoning scripts/schemas/planning.json states for `focus`: an empty policy means readable by every member of the org, no row scope, and PINNED — a type's own `access` REPLACES the org-wide `*` default wholesale, so a later org-wide posture cannot silently narrow the one type every scoped read resolves through. A tenant that must hide scopes from some members declares row_scope here having read the orphaning warning in access.py; it is NOT the default, because a scope switcher that silently loses half its tree reads as data loss. The SCOPE-AWARE READ GATE — staff see every scope, a client user sees one — is bd startsim-lyqyd and mirrors row_scope_exempt_*; it is not this key.

attributes.name: name
attributes.note: What a person calls it: 'OGMC', 'GCC Weekly'. Duplicates Entity.name on purpose, for the same reason planning.json's `title` does: Entity.name carries display and search, the attribute carries queryability and ordering, and only declared attributes get the core_attribute rows that are filterable at all.

attributes.name: kind
attributes.note: THE LABEL A PERSON USES, and PRESENTATIONAL ONLY — never a query gate. Nothing in the server branches on it: a scope's place in the tree is its `path`, and a filter that read `kind` would reintroduce the client-vs-project split this type exists to remove. A tenant whose vernacular needs a fourth word extends `choices` with a config PATCH; that is a data change, not a migration.

attributes.name: path
attributes.note: THE MATERIALIZED PATH, and the whole query mechanism: `/ogmc`, `/ogmc/gcc-weekly`. Leading separator always; no trailing one (filters.normalize_container corrects a caller's trailing slash, but stored values carry none). TEXT and never longtext or json: `__under` is a range scan on value_text and refuses any other column outright, and values longer than core.search.MAX_FILTERABLE_TEXT_CHARS fall outside the partial index the filter repeats the predicate of. Named by this type's own `config.scope.path_attribute`, which is what makes the scope type navigable by the same `?scope=` every other type uses.

attributes.name: parent
attributes.note: The PARENT's path, or EMPTY for a root. REDUNDANT WITH `path` BY CONSTRUCTION — it is `path` minus its last segment — and stored anyway because a tree UI filters `?attr.parent=/ogmc` for direct children without deriving anything, and because a mismatch between the two is a detectable corruption rather than an invisible one. THE EMPTY SPELLING FOR A ROOT IS LOAD-BEARING AND WAS MEASURED, not assumed: denormalize_attributes writes a core_attribute row for a declared key whose value is the empty string, so `?attr.parent=` is a real filter that returns exactly the top-level scopes — the first query a scope switcher issues. A root storing `/` instead would leave 'list the clients' with no spelling but an anti-join over the whole type. Note that scoping.ancestors() tops out at `/` rather than at `` — the resolution root is not the stored parent value, and the one conversion between them is documented on that function. It is NOT the subtree mechanism either way: a chain of `parent` reads is the depth-capped walk the path exists to replace.

attributes.name: active
attributes.note: Whether work still happens here. A boolean and not a status enum, because 'paused', 'churned' and 'archived' are things a person tracks ABOUT a client rather than things the pipeline branches on — and the pipeline needs exactly one bit. Absent means active: a scope nobody has answered the question about is not thereby switched off.

attributes.name: brand_voice
attributes.note: INHERITED. How this scope sounds. longtext because it is the paragraph an LLM is actually handed, and it lives on the RECORD rather than in n8n prompt text — which is where OGMC's lived, and is why every other client's copy would have been written in OGMC's voice. Empty means 'ask my parent' (see inheritance_note); it does not mean 'no voice'.

attributes.name: priority_framework
attributes.note: INHERITED. What this scope considers worth covering — the rubric the classifier and the judge apply. This is the field whose absence made the whole corpus implicitly OGMC's: a sports client scored against a GCC construction rubric gets a plausible answer to the wrong question, which is the failure that is hardest to see.

attributes.name: guardrails
attributes.note: INHERITED. What must never be said or done for this scope. INHERITANCE IS A UNION IN SPIRIT AND A SINGLE VALUE IN STORAGE: a child that declares its own guardrails REPLACES its parent's rather than adding to them, exactly as every other inherited field does, so a child overriding this must restate what it still needs. Stated here because 'the child adds a rule' is the reading a person expects and it is not the one the resolver implements.

attributes.name: services
attributes.note: INHERITED. What this scope is actually delivered — the engagement, in the words the deliverable is written against.

relationships.label: Draft in scope
relationships.note: LIVE_RELATIONSHIPS in tenant-starter/apps/api/tests/test_agent_account_isolation.py, and the edge the draft type's own config.scope.edge names. ONE PER SCOPED SOURCE TYPE, which is why it is not called `in_scope`: RelationshipDef carries UniqueConstraint(['org_id','key']) and RelationshipViewSet._validate_edge_types resolves a reldef by KEY alone, so an org holds at most one `in_scope` bound to one concrete (source,target) pair and a second scoped type sending it is refused for having the wrong source type (scoping.py's EDGE_KEY note). STRUCTURE ONLY: subtree membership is answered by attr.scope_path__under over the materialized path and MUST NOT be answered by walking this, because related_depth caps at 2 and a client with projects under it is already depth 3. The edge and the path attribute are written together on upsert (bd startsim-j0ew2) because either alone is a half-truth the other cannot repair.

relationships.label: Grounded by
relationships.note: LIVE_RELATIONSHIPS (2026-09-16 capture), and in the 2026-08-19 ECS-exec reading's rel-def list. The evidence edge from a topic back to the curated news it was generated from — the pipeline stage start-simpli-api/backend/apps/foundry/watch_declarations/ogmc.json calls the 'Topic-strategist pool (status=acceptable)' draining into topics-all and news-cited.

COPIED VERBATIM FROM scripts/schemas/scope.json, and present in the 2026-09-16 capture. A scope nests under a parent scope. Direction is CHILD -> PARENT (the child is the edge's SOURCE), matching planning.json's `sub_focus` and central's Goal.parent, so a child names its parent. READ IT THE WAY filters._one_hop DEFINES IT, because the obvious reading is backwards: `related_direction` describes the RETURNED ROW's end of the edge, not the direction you are walking — so the CHILDREN of a scope are ?related_to=<parentId>&related_via=parent_scope&related_direction=out, and a scope's PARENT is the same query with related_direction=in. STRUCTURE ONLY. This edge exists for the UI, the schema builder and RelationshipDef validation. Subtree membership is `?scope=` over the materialized path and MUST NOT be answered by walking this, because related_depth caps at 2 and a client with projects under it is already depth 3.
